'''Kirsten "Kiki" Sanford''' is an American [[neurophysiology|neurophysiologist]] and [[Science communication|science communicator]]. After working at the [[University of California, Davis]] as a research scientist,<ref name="Science Resume at The Bird's Brain">{{cite web|url=http://www.kirstensanford.com/science-resume/|title=Science Resume|work=kirstensanford.com|date=November 12, 2007|access-date=August 25, 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150825154509/http://www.kirstensanford.com/science-resume/|archivedate=August 25, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> she left research work to pursue a career in science communication. Her work has included multiple audio and video programs, including the ''This Week in Science'' radio program and podcast and ''Dr. Kiki's Science Hour'', a podcast involving interviews with experts in a given scientific field.<ref name="twis.org">{{cite web|url=https://www.twis.org/|title=This Week in Science – The Kickass Science Podcast|work=twis.org|access-date=August 25, 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180914101636/https://www.twis.org/|archivedate=September 14, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="dksh">{{cite web|url=https://twit.tv/shows/dr-kikis-science-hour|title=Dr. Kiki's Science Hour|work=twit.tv|access-date=August 25, 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150825155305/https://twit.tv/shows/dr-kikis-science-hour|archivedate=August 25, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Sanford was born in [[Santa Rosa, California]] and raised near Stockton, California.<ref name="TVWeek">{{cite web|title=Kirsten "Dr. Kiki" Sanford, Host and Science Expert|url=http://www.tvweek.com/talking-tv/dealmakers/2008/04/kirsten_dr_kiki_sanford_host_a.php|work=Digital Dealmakers|publisher=TVWeek|date=April 13, 2008|accessdate=August 25, 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140529125934/http://www.tvweek.com/talking-tv/dealmakers/2008/04/kirsten_dr_kiki_sanford_host_a.php|archivedate=May 29, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> She holds a B.S. in [[conservation biology]] and Ph.D. in [[systems biology|Molecular, Cellular, and Integrative Physiology]] from U.C. Davis. She is a specialist in learning and memory.<ref name="Science Resume at The Bird's Brain"/> While attending graduate school at U.C. Davis, she found academic bureaucracy unappealing and decided to shift her career path from research to science communication.<ref name="TVWeek"/> Sanford holds a black belt in [[taekwondo]].<ref name="asylum">{{cite web|last=Lewinski|first=John|title=Dr. Kiki Sanford Can Kick Our Ass and Talk Over Our Heads ... and We're in Love|url=http://www.asylum.com/2010/03/29/dr-kirsten-kiki-sanford-this-week-in-science/|publisher=Asylum|work=Today's Crush|date=March 29, 2010|accessdate=August 25, 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140820031611/http://www.asylum.com/2010/03/29/dr-kirsten-kiki-sanford-this-week-in-science/|archivedate=August 20, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> She says martial arts was "something concrete to escape to" when faced with research hardships during graduate school.<ref name="asylum"/> Sanford lived in San Francisco with her husband until moving to Portland, Oregon in April 2015.<ref name="TVWeek" /><ref name="pdx">{{cite tweet|number=591297421956775937|user=drkiki|title=Hi there @OMSI! I just moved to Portland and would love to collaborate on some science outreach.|date=April 23, 2015|access-date=August 25, 2015}}</ref>

==Science communication==
[[Image:Kiki Sanford at SkeptiCal.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Sanford podcasts at SkeptiCal - Berkeley, CA - April 21, 2012|alt=A woman smiling toward the camera]]
Sanford, known as "Dr. Kiki," produces and appears in a number of science education programs. Sanford says of her work, "My shtick is: Dr. Kiki reaches out to people who don't necessarily like science to get them to see it as something enjoyable. My goal is to get people who maybe flunked chemistry or didn't do well on their science fair project to say, 'This is really interesting.'"<ref name="TVWeek" />

Sanford is the host and editor of the ''This Week in Science'' radio show/podcast, which she founded in 1999. ''This Week in Science'' is a weekly program formerly streamed live from the [[TWiT.tv|This Week in Tech Network]] (TWiT), and then rebroadcast from U.C. Davis' [[KDVS]], 90.3 FM.<ref name="twis.org"/> ''This Week in Science'' currently records every Wednesday night using [[Google+#Hangouts and Hangouts On-Air|Hangouts on Air]] which are streamed live on both YouTube and the ''This Week in Science'' live page.

Starting in late 2007, Sanford expanded her work, starring in On Network's successful series ''Food Science''. The program explores the science of cooking as well as at-home experiments involving food.<ref name="prweb">{{cite web|last=Fraser|first=Denise|title=ON Networks Introduces New Food Line-up That's Sure to Tantalize Tastebuds|url=http://www.prweb.com/releases/networks/science/prweb547529.htm|publisher=[[PR Web]]|date=August 17, 2007|access-date=August 25, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150825162458/http://www.prweb.com/releases/networks/science/prweb547529.htm|archive-date=August 25, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2008, she began co-hosting [[Revision3]]'s variety show ''PopSiren''.<ref name="TVWeek" /><ref name="wired">{{cite magazine|last=Lewinski|first=John|title=Mr. Wizard Muscled Out by Sexier Redhead Scientist|url=https://www.wired.com/2008/05/her-name-might/|magazine=[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]]|accessdate=August 25, 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150825162605/http://www.wired.com/2008/05/her-name-might/|archivedate=August 25, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> ''PopSiren'' described itself as offering a "feminine perspective" on pop culture and technology.<ref name="rev3">{{cite web|title=PopSiren homepage|url=http://revision3.com/popsiren|publisher=[[Revision3]]|accessdate=August 25, 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150825163002/http://revision3.com/popsiren|archivedate=August 25, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In May 2008, Sanford along with several other skeptics and scientists created a pilot for a TV series titled ''The Skeptologists''. The premise was that claimed experts in a field of [[pseudoscience]] or the [[paranormal]] would present their claims, which would then be investigated by the team.<ref name="skeptologists">{{cite web|url=http://www.skeptologists.com/|title=TV SERIES|work=The Skeptologists|accessdate=August 25, 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150825181202/http://www.skeptologists.com/|archivedate=August 25, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>

On April 30, 2009, ''Dr. Kiki's Science Hour'' started broadcasting on TWiT.tv. The show, recorded live on TWiT, became a podcast with episode 24. Guests included scientists, [[scientific skepticism|skeptics]], and science communicators such as astronomer [[Phil Plait]] and neurologist [[Steven Novella]].<ref name="discoverplait">{{cite web|last=Plait|authorlink=Phil Plait|first=Phil|title=I'm guest hosting Dr. Kiki's Science Hour on Thursday!|url=http://blogs.discovermagazine.com/badastronomy/2011/03/16/im-guest-hosting-dr-kikis-science-hour-on-thursday/|work=Bad Astronomy|publisher=[[Discover (magazine)|Discover]]|date=March 16, 2011|accessdate=August 25, 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150825163405/http://blogs.discovermagazine.com/badastronomy/2011/03/16/im-guest-hosting-dr-kikis-science-hour-on-thursday/|archivedate=August 25, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="dksh33">{{cite web|title=Retracting The Needle From Autism|url=https://twit.tv/shows/dr-kikis-science-hour/episodes/33|work=Dr. Kiki's Science Hour|publisher=[[TWiT.tv]]|date=February 5, 2010|accessdate=August 25, 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150825163931/https://twit.tv/shows/dr-kikis-science-hour/episodes/33|archivedate=August 25, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> The last episode aired on June 29, 2012. While at TWiT she also co-hosted ''Green Tech Today'', a show about [[environmentally friendly]] technology, and ''Science News Weekly'' a five-minute show.<ref name="gtt">{{cite web|url=https://twit.tv/shows/green-tech-today|title=Green Tech Today|publisher=[[TWiT.tv]]|accessdate=August 25, 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150825181731/https://twit.tv/shows/green-tech-today|archivedate=August 25, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="snw">{{cite web|url=https://twit.tv/shows/science-news-weekly|title=Science News Weekly|publisher=[[TWiT.tv]]|accessdate=August 25, 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150825181841/https://twit.tv/shows/science-news-weekly|archivedate=August 25, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>

Sanford has produced and hosted various segments for [[The Science Channel]]'s science program ''Brink''.<ref name="Media Resume">{{cite web|title=Dr. Kiki Sanford Media Resume|url=http://www.kirstensanford.com/media-resume/|date=November 12, 2007|work=kirstensanford.com|accessdate=August 25, 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150825164225/http://www.kirstensanford.com/media-resume/|archivedate=August 25, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>

In February 2015, Sanford launched a new company to help researchers and other scientists have better communication. The company, named ''Broader Impacts'', does video production and social media outreach.<ref name="broaderimpacts">{{cite web|url=http://www.broaderimpacts.tv/|title=Broader Impacts|accessdate=August 25, 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150825183455/http://www.broaderimpacts.tv/|archivedate=August 25, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Awards==
In 2005, Sanford was awarded the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] Mass Media Science & Engineering Fellowship, in recognition for her work with her radio show ''This Week in Science''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://php.aaas.org/programs/education/MassMedia/alumniDisplay.php|title=AAAS Mass Media Science & Engineering Fellows Program|publisher=[[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130508175629/http://php.aaas.org/programs/education/MassMedia/alumniDisplay.php|archivedate=May 8, 2013|url-status=dead|access-date=August 25, 2015}}</ref> Through the fellowship she worked as a television news producer at [[WNBC]] News in [[New York City]], alongside noted health and science reporter [[Max Gomez]].<ref name="Media Resume" />
